vignette: Ravi, a 61-year-old South Asian man with salt-and-pepper hair and deep, expressive eyes, works as a non-profit worker advocating for underprivileged communities. His role involves frequent travel to different parts of the state, often driving long distances to meet community leaders and stakeholders. Despite his dedication and passion for his job, Ravi's life has been irrevocably altered by a near-fatal motor vehicle collision that occurred three months ago. The accident happened on one of those typical drives to an outreach event in a neighboring town. It was raining heavily, and the roads were slick with water. As Ravi approached a sharp turn, he lost control of his car. The skid sent him careening into a guardrail, and for a moment, time seemed to slow down as he braced himself for impact. Miraculously, Ravi survived with only minor injuries-bruises and cuts-but the event left an indelible mark on his psyche. Since then, driving has become a daunting task. Every time Ravi gets behind the wheel, the memories flood back. He often finds himself hyperventilating and breaking out in cold sweats as he anticipates another collision. Even minor bumps or sudden noises can trigger intense panic attacks. The fear is so pervasive that he avoids driving altogether whenever possible, opting to use public transportation despite its inconvenience for his work schedule. At night, the nightmares begin. He dreams of being trapped in a spinning car, unable to control it as it hurtles toward an inevitable crash. These nightmares leave him drenched in sweat and gasping for air, leading to sleepless nights that he attempts to cope with through excessive caffeine consumption during the day. His wife has noticed his erratic sleep patterns but struggles to understand how deeply the accident has affected him. Ravi's emotional state is fragile; any reminder of the event can send him into a tailspin. The sound of screeching tires, the sight of a red emergency vehicle, or even the smell of gasoline can trigger flashbacks that leave him feeling disoriented and overwhelmed. He often experiences vivid recollections of the moment he lost control, replaying it over and over in his mind as if trying to find an alternative outcome. His work has also been impacted. The accident happened during a particularly critical phase of a project aimed at providing healthcare access to rural areas. Despite his best efforts, Ravi's performance has declined. He finds himself distracted and unable to concentrate on meetings or reports. Simple tasks that once came easily now seem insurmountable. Colleagues have commented on his absent-mindedness, but Ravi remains tight-lipped about the true source of his distress. Ravi's wife is increasingly concerned. She notices how he clings to her presence, seeking reassurance that everything will be okay. He has grown more irritable and short-tempered at home, lashing out in frustration over minor issues. Conversations often veer toward the accident, with Ravi repeatedly questioning whether he could have done something differently. Despite his best intentions, Ravi is struggling to maintain a semblance of normalcy. The once vibrant man now seems quieter, more withdrawn. He avoids social gatherings and even refuses invitations from colleagues who want to meet for coffee or lunch. His sense of self-worth has diminished, and he questions whether he can ever fully recover. As Ravi navigates this new reality, the memories of that fateful day continue to haunt him, shaping every aspect of his life-from how he works to how he interacts with loved ones. The road ahead is uncertain, but for now, Ravi holds on to hope, hoping one day he will be able to reclaim a sense of peace and control over his life.
